A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same discrete diffusion sampler and convergence analysis. The main text and Appendices A–E are readable, and corresponding theorems, proofs, Table 1, Figure 1, and Algorithm 1 can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes. Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Its added application examples and implementation discussion do not report empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds an optional procedural alternative: obtain the uniformization rate from a computable clipping-based upper bound instead of exact maximization over all states. The score objective, time discretization, and main sampling construction remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or evaluation. The added text, image, and protein examples in Section 4 illustrate the retained state-space formulation rather than extend evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparisons with Chen and Ying (2024). Neither version evaluates empirical baselines, and the updated DNDM citation refers to the same method.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental evaluation protocols, data splits, training budgets, or testing procedures. The sampling-rate clarification concerns implementation of the theoretical algorithm.

E4.justification: Neither version contains ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity studies, or empirical case analyses. The appendix revisions concern mathematical proofs and sampling implementation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or empirical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. Table 1 retains the same convergence bounds, and Appendix D's sampling-complexity expressions (27)–(30) already appear in v1.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the reverse-generator indices and time arguments, and Appendix A.2 corrects an inner summation limit from d to S. Appendix A.1 adds explicit Kronecker-sum verification. Proposition 3 removes its separate error-equivalence statement and revises the proof of the retained Bregman inequality. The principal assumptions and convergence bounds remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its priority claim for exponential convergence of the forward process, changing 'we first derive' to 'we derive.' The central contributions concerning discrete-time sampling, early stopping, and nearly dimension-linear convergence remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 5 removes v1's claim of substantially faster sampling through fewer network evaluations and acknowledges that score clipping aligns with Chen and Ying's bounded-estimator assumption. It also adds a fully supported i.i.d. example for Assumption 2. The conclusion's existing limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v1 already supplies the score-clipping bound in its complexity discussion. v2 explicitly explains how to use it to choose the uniformization rate without enumerating S^d states, providing actionable implementation guidance in Appendix D.

R1.justification: v2 adds Trippe et al. (2023), removes the separate Guo et al. (2023) listing while retaining Guo et al. (2024), and qualifies its advantages relative to Chen and Ying. The DNDM title and publication update identifies the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and terminology edits, integrates the Contributions and Notation subsections into the introduction, adds acknowledgements and explanatory passages, and streamlines Appendix E. The overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into the ICLR template, changing typography, text width, spacing, title and author arrangement, and running headers. Table 1 and Figure 1 are resized and repositioned, and Algorithm 1 moves relative to Appendix C.4; their substantive visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision through mathematical corrections, clearer implementation guidance in Appendix D, and a more qualified comparison with Chen and Ying in Section 5. These changes reduce ambiguity and overstatement while preserving the principal guarantees. The gains are limited refinements rather than a substantial change in the paper's theoretical contribution.
